Editorial
The context responsible for authoring, reviewing, and publishing articles. Owns the article lifecycle from draft to published; hands off to at the publish boundary.
Editorial is where prose becomes a published artifact. It models the workflow editors actually run — write, review, revise, publish — and deliberately stops short of distribution mechanics (RSS, syndication, CDN warmup), which live downstream.
src/editorial/** src/shared/markdown/**
Article
A unit of editorial work with a stable identity across revisions. An article persists through title changes, slug changes, and full rewrites; what changes is its content, not its identity.
Identity is decoupled from slug so that URL changes don't fork the article's history. See .
Stable by article-id (uuid v7). Slug and title are mutable attributes, not identity.
Slug
The URL-safe identifier under which an article is published. Kebab-case, lowercase ASCII, max 80 characters.
Two slugs are equal when their normalized string forms are byte-equal. Case is normalized to lowercase before comparison.
publishArticle

A event on success, or a structured validation failure listing unmet preconditions.
ArticlePublished
A fact: the editorial team has promoted an article to the public surface. Past tense; immutable once emitted.
succeeds and the article transitions from draft to published state.
article-id, slug at publish time, published-at timestamp, reviewer-id of the approving editor.
EditorialReview
The collaborative act of an editor reading a draft and either approving it for publication or returning it with notes. Not an entity (no stable identity) and not a value (carries state); a named concept that recurs in conversation about the workflow.
Surfaced as a named concept because the team consistently refers to "review" as a discrete step, even though it isn't reified as a single record in the data model.
Byline
The author-attribution string rendered above an article. Replaced by structured author references in v3; kept here to document the term for historical contexts.
Two bylines are equal when their string forms match exactly, including whitespace.
Drafts cannot be published without review
must reject any that lacks an approving from an editor other than the article's author.
Self-review defeats the purpose; the rule must hold at the code boundary, not by convention.
Slug must match the canonical shape
Every persisted must match the pattern ^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{0,79}$. Enforced by a lint rule on the schema migrations directory.
Catches malformed slugs at PR time rather than at request time, where a 404 would already have been served.
Slug is mutable; identity is not
An 's slug may change over its lifetime; its article-id may not. Downstream systems that need a stable handle must use article-id, not slug.
Slugs reflect editorial intent (a renamed article gets a renamed URL); identity reflects the underlying artifact. Conflating them would force every rename to fork the article's history.
Editorial → Distribution
Editorial supplies the published-article stream; Distribution consumes it. Distribution can request schema changes; Editorial negotiates and ships them.
Downstream pull works because the two teams meet weekly and the contract is small.
Editorial → Legacy CMS
Editorial accepts the legacy CMS's content schema as-is; no translation layer.
Editorial ← Vendor Imports
Incoming vendor content passes through a translation layer that maps vendor fields onto editorial's vocabulary; vendor concepts never leak past the boundary.
Editorial Public API
A stable HTTP surface that any downstream context may consume without negotiation.
Identity kernel
Editorial and Distribution co-own the user-id and author-id value types; changes require both contexts' agreement.
ArticlePublished event schema
The event payload is a versioned, published contract. Any consumer may read it; changes go through a deprecation cycle.
Editorial ↔ Reader Profiles
The two contexts succeed or fail together on personalized recommendations; coordinated planning is the norm, not the exception.
Editorial ⊥ Marketing Site
No integration. The marketing site re-implements whatever it needs from scratch rather than depending on editorial.
Editorial ? Archive
A historical integration whose shape predates this lexicon; the contract is undocumented and the owning team is gone. Marked unknown until someone investigates.
Draft articles must not be readable from any context outside Editorial, regardless of caller identity or feature flag.
A draft leaking to distribution would be indistinguishable from a publish; rolling it back after the fact is expensive and visible.
Article aggregate
Article is the consistency boundary: slug changes and review state transitions commit together with article updates, never independently.
Publishing pipeline
The atoms involved in moving an article from draft to published, grouped because they cohere as a single workflow even though they span entity, service, and event categories.
Named so that conversation and crystallizations can refer to "the publishing pipeline" without re-enumerating its members each time.
